sites.name: Trinity River Campground
sites.operator: Forest Service · run by shasta recreation company
sites.feeText: Overnight Use: Single Site: $16 per night Additional Vehicle Fee: $8 per vehicle per night
sites.waterText: Water can be treated or filtered from nearby water sources
sites.about: The Trinity River campground is located two miles north of the Coffee Creek area on Highway 3, and lies on the banks of the Trinity River. It is approximately 36 miles from Weaverville. It is very popular with travelers as an overnight campground as it is located on Highway 3. This facility has a…
sites.directions: From Weaverville, take Hwy 3 north for 38 miles. Campground is on the left side of Hwy 3.

sites.name: Goldfield Campground
sites.feeText: No fees are required for this site
sites.waterText: Water can be treated or filtered from nearby water sources
sites.about: This campground is closed after being burnt in the River Complex Fires. It is expected to be re-built but is now closed.
sites.directions: From Weaverville, take Hwy 3 north for 36.6 miles. Turn left onto the Coffee Creek Road for 4.7 miles. Turn left onto bridge over Coffee Creek to the campground.

sites.name: Preacher Meadow Campground
sites.operator: Forest Service · run by shasta recreation company
sites.feeText: Overnight Use: Single Site: $20 per night
sites.about: Quiet and serene this campground attracts hikers as it is near the popular Swift Creek trailhead and many persons stay there before and after their hikes. The campground has two large unnamed loops meandering through mature cedar, ponderosa pine and some deciduous trees. Each campsite has a…
sites.directions: From Weaverville, take Hwy 3 north for 27 miles. Turn left at the campground sign. Campground is 1/2 mile from the turnoff.

sites.name: Jackass Springs Campground
sites.feeText: No fees are required for this site
sites.waterText: Water can be treated or filtered from nearby water sources
sites.about: This remote campground on the east side of Trinity Lake offers 10 campsites that can accommodate a trailer up to 32'.
sites.directions: From Weaverville, take Hwy 3 north for 34.2 miles. Turn right on County Road 106, crossing over Carrville Bridge. Stay on County Road 106 for 12.4 miles until Jackass Springs Road junction. Turn…

sites.name: Eagle Creek Campground
sites.operator: Forest Service · run by shasta recreation company
sites.feeText: Overnight Use: Single Site: $16 per night Additional Vehicle Fee: $8 per vehicle per night
sites.waterText: Water can be treated or filtered from nearby water sources
sites.about: This campground is located on the northside of Trinity Lake along State Highway 3 approximately five miles north of the Coffee Creek area and is surrounded by the Trinity River on one side and Eagle Creek on the other. It mostly attracts tent campers, but has several trailer length spurs. There…
sites.directions: From Weaverville, take Hwy 3 north for 40.9 miles. Take the second Eagle Creek Loop Road turnoff. Turn right at the T-intersection for 1.1 miles to the campground.

sites.name: Horse Flat Campground
sites.feeText: No fees are required for this site
sites.waterText: Water can be treated or filtered from nearby water sources
sites.about: This campground offers 10 units that can accommodate trailers up to 16 feet. There is no piped water. There are several more sites by the creek across the main road. The Eagle Creek Trail leaves from this campground.
sites.directions: From Weaverville, take Hwy 3 north for 40.9 miles. Take the second Eagle Creek Loop Road turnoff. Turn right at the T-intersection. Pass Eagle Creek Campground. Continue on dirt road for 2 miles to…

sites.name: Clear Creek Campground
sites.feeText: No fees are required for this site
sites.waterText: Water can be treated or filtered from nearby water sources
sites.about: Clear Creek campground is a small remote facility with only 6 campsites. It can accommodate a trailer up to 22 feet and offers picnic tables, fire rings and a vault toilet.
